newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-WEAH GOAL PUTS LIBERIA BACK IN FRAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEAH GOAL PUTS LIBERIA BACK IN FRAME.

text.p: George Weah scored a rare international goal to revive Liberia's outside hopes of a first appearance in the World Cup finals on a hectic weekend of qualifiers in Africa.
The Milan striker's first-half effort against Egypt, thundered home from 20 metres, gave Liberia their first win of the qualifying campaign.
A trio of other Europe-based forwards also made significant contributions.
Daniel Amokachi of Turkish club Besiktas doubled his tally of World Cup goals with two more for Nigeria in their 2-1 home win over Guinea in Lagos.
Belgium-based Mike Okoth Origi scored a second-half hat-trick to give Kenya a 4-3 victory against Burkina Faso after trailing 2-0 at halftime.
In the Congo on Sunday, Macchembe Younga struck twice in six minutes to give the hosts an upset 2-0 win over African champions South Africa in Pointe Noire.
The Fortuna Duesseldorf striker stepped off the plane on the morning of the match after playing in a Bundesliga game against St Pauli on Saturday to put Congo three points clear in group three.
The weekend was marred by a riot in Libreville which saw Ugandan referee Charles Massembe abandon the match between Gabon and Morocco.

Two goals each from Morocco's Saudi-based frontline of Ahmed Bahja and Bassir Salaheddine had the visitors 4-0 up. It was too much for the home crowd to stomach and rioting saw Massembe call a halt after 55 minutes.
Morocco are likely to be given the three points, which will put them well on course to qualify from group five, while Gabon will face the wrath of FIFA.
Despite Weah ending an 18 months goal drought for his country with a 26th minute score that enabled Liberia to jump over Egypt in group two, Tunisia still look the hot favourite to advance.

The north Africans lead the standings with nine points and a 100 percent record after winning 2-1 in Namibia. Goals by Taoufik Hicheri and substitute Khlaed Badra ended the hosts' 10-game unbeaten home run.
Liberia must win in Tunis when the teams meet on April 27.
Nigeria's win on Saturday sees them ahead in group one but it proved another close call for the Super Eagles, playing their first game under new coach Philippe Troussier.
Kenya were two goals down to Burkina Faso at halftime in Nairobi but Origi's treble spurred them to a 4-3 win that keeps alive thier faint hopes of toppling the Nigerians in the group.
Cameroon and Angola kept up their fight for top spot in group four with the Indomitable Lions beating Zimbabwe 1-0 and Angola coming from behind to beat Togo 3-1 in Luanda.
The Benfica duo of Paulao and Akwa scored the first two for the Angolans with Sousa hitting his first international goal in the second-half.
Both teams have seven points from three games.
Ghana, another team with a new coach, played to a third successive draw in group five, this time away to Sierra Leone in Freetown.

The Black Stars, now coached by Dutchman Rinus Israel, led after an own goal by defender Abubakari Kamara but then conceded a late equaliser. Should Morocco be awarded the points from their abandoned game they will be four clear of Ghana, who trail Sierra Leone by a point.
The weekend marked the halfway point in the qualifying campaign and all 20 teams return to action in three weeks' time.
